memories.text: Structure empirical papers as Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion.
Write abstracts of about 150 words that state the question, method, main result and implication, with no citations.
IEEE style numbers references in square brackets in order of first appearance.
Write methods in the past tense and general truths in the present tense.
Every figure needs a self-contained caption and axis labels with units.
Format tables without vertical lines, put units in the column headers, and align numbers on the decimal point.
A paper title states the finding or the object studied, in under 15 words.
Write the cover letter: state the contribution in two sentences, suggest three reviewers, and declare conflicts of interest.

fields.trigger: submit a manuscript to a journal
steps: state the contribution in two sentences
confirm the paper is not under review elsewhere

memories.text: Answer reviewers point by point: quote each comment, say what changed and where, and be polite when disagreeing.

steps: say what changed and where in the manuscript

memories.text: A manuscript was desk-rejected for exceeding the word limit; read the author guidelines before writing.

fields.situation: a paper is rejected immediately without review
fields.insight: it exceeded the journal's word limit

memories.text: For double-blind submissions remove author names and citations that identify yourself.
Use the journal's LaTeX template and manage the bibliography with biblatex in the journal's style.
Order authors by contribution and agree it at the start of the project using the CRediT roles.
Keep all references in Zotero with the DOI filled in; never type a bibliography by hand.
Check the journal's word limit before submitting the manuscript.
